title: Fate of dynamical quantum phase transitions from sudden quench to slow quench limit
abstract: Previous investigations of dynamical quantum phase transition (DQPT) have predominantly focused on sudden quench protocols. In this work, we systematically explore the fate of DQPT from the sudden to the slow quench regime. We establish that DQPT remains robust under slow quenching when the protocol crosses an equilibrium quantum phase transition. Conversely, we show that accidental DQPTs,which occur when the pre and post quench Hamiltonians reside in the same equilibrium phase, can be filtered out in the slow quench limit. This demonstrates that slow quenches can reveal the intrinsic connection between DQPT and equilibrium quantum phase transitions, thereby enabling DQPT to serve as a dynamical probe for identifying equilibrium quantum critical points. We illustrate these findings with examples from the XY chain, the Aubry-André model, and the trimer Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model.
summary: This paper explores the fate of Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions by comparing sudden and slow quenching protocols. It demonstrates that while sudden quenches can show spurious transitions, only slow quenches reveal DQPTs intrinsically linked to true equilibrium quantum phase transitions. This establishes a robust method for using non-equilibrium dynamics as a probe for identifying critical points.
main_problem: The study systematically investigates how Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions (DQPTs) behave when the quench protocol is varied from a sudden switch to a slow, adiabatic-like change.
main_result: Slow quenches can distinguish intrinsic DQPTs—those linked to equilibrium quantum phase transitions—from 'accidental' ones that occur within a single equilibrium phase.
method: The analysis relies on calculating the Loschmidt echo and its associated rate function, comparing results obtained from sudden versus slow quench protocols across various models.
model_or_system: The work applies to general 1D two-band models, specifically analyzing the XY chain, the Aubry-André model, and the trimer Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH3) model. The dynamics are governed by time-dependent Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Loschmidt echo ($L(t)$), rate function ($r(t)$), and nonanalyticities in $r(t)$ which signal a DQPT.
important_parameters: The quench rate ($ eta$), the initial and final Hamiltonian parameters ($h_i, h_f$), and the crossing of an equilibrium quantum phase transition are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: It is assumed that slow quenches reveal the intrinsic connection between DQPTs and underlying equilibrium quantum criticality, provided a bulk gap closure occurs during the process.
figures_summary: Figures compare rate functions $r(t)$ for sudden versus slow quenches in the SSH3 model, demonstrating how the slow quench filters out spurious transitions and reveals scaling laws related to critical exponents.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general framework using Loschmidt echoes, then contrasting the results of sudden vs. slow quenches, and finally applying this rigorous test to multiple physical models (XY chain, Aubry-André, SSH3) to confirm the theoretical predictions.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful diagnostic tool—the slow quench limit—to rigorously connect non-equilibrium dynamics (DQPTs) directly to static critical points (QPTs), which is highly relevant for understanding quantum criticality in driven systems.
